dialogue.speaker: James
dialogue.text: Do you have a few minutes? I would like some feedback on my presentation.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Of course. First of all, the structure was clear and your examples were interesting.

dialogue.speaker: James
dialogue.text: Thank you. And what could I improve?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I have a suggestion: try to speak more slowly, especially at the beginning.

dialogue.speaker: James
dialogue.text: I did feel nervous. Was it really noticeable?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: A little, but it is easy to fix. A short pause between the main points would help.

dialogue.speaker: James
dialogue.text: Anything else? Please be honest. I can take criticism.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The final slides had too much text, so the audience started reading instead of listening.

dialogue.speaker: James
dialogue.text: That is helpful. Could you be more specific about which slides?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Slides eight and nine. Use one image and one sentence instead.

dialogue.speaker: James
dialogue.text: I will do that. Honestly, I was afraid it had gone badly.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Not at all. You have made real progress since your last presentation.

dialogue.speaker: James
dialogue.text: That really motivates me to keep practicing.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good. Constructive feedback should motivate people, not discourage them.

dialogue.speaker: James
dialogue.text: Agreed. Would you like me to give you feedback on yours next week?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I would be grateful. Thank you for being open to it.
